title: Hidden Temporal Coupling (Sequential API Dependencies)
pattern: An object exposing multiple public methods that must be executed in a strict chronological sequence, but whose type signatures do not enforce this sequence via compile-time constraints.
why_bad: This design counts on other programmers guessing the undocumented sequence perfectly [411:411]. It creates hidden temporal coupling where changing the order leads to catastrophic runtime failures or silent memory corruption [395:395].
detection: API classes exposing stateful builder methods that panic or produce undefined behavior when invoked in alternative orderings [410:410].
fix: Expose state transformations through a "bucket brigade" structure where each method consumes the previous state and returns a new distinct type, forcing correct sequential execution at compile time [411:411].
